name: mremap
synopsis: void *mremap(void *old_address, size_t old_size, size_t new_size, int flags, ... /* void *new_address */);
description: mremap() expands or shrinks an existing memory mapping, potentially relocating it based on flags and available virtual address space. It requires the original address and sizes, and can optionally specify a new address for relocation.

parameters.name: old_address
parameters.description: The old address of the virtual memory block to expand or shrink; must be page-aligned.

parameters.name: old_size
parameters.description: The old size of the virtual memory block.

parameters.name: new_size
parameters.description: The requested new size of the virtual memory block after resizing.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: A bit-mask of flags, such as MREMAP_MAYMOVE, MREMAP_FIXED, or MREMAP_DONTUNMAP, to control behavior.

parameters.name: new_address
parameters.description: Optional fifth argument; specifies a page-aligned address to move the mapping to, used with MREMAP_FIXED.

return_value.success: Returns a pointer to the new virtual memory area
return_value.failure: Returns MAP_FAILED (that is, (void*)-1) and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: The caller tried to expand a locked memory segment, but it exceeded the RLIMIT_MEMLOCK resource limit.
An invalid virtual memory address exists in the range old_address to old_address + old_size.
An invalid argument was provided, such as non-page-aligned old_address, invalid flags, zero new_size, or other conditions like overlapping ranges.
Not enough memory was available to complete the operation, possibly due to inability to expand or relocate the mapping.

bugs: Before Linux 4.14, if old_size was zero and the mapping was private, mremap() created a new private mapping unrelated to the original, which was unintended; since Linux 4.14, it fails with EINVAL in this scenario.
versions: Available since Linux 2.3.31, with MREMAP_FIXED added in Linux 2.3.31 and MREMAP_DONTUNMAP in Linux 5.7; prior to glibc 2.4, glibc did not expose MREMAP_FIXED.
